end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Compared apples from Shimla (350 km) with spinach (15–20 km) as a longer versus shorter journey.
Linked longer journeys with more fuel use, pollution, refrigeration, packaging and plastic waste.
Final teach-back was not passed; the definition was repeated and expanded during the lesson.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, comparing travel distances, and explaining effects on fuel, pollution, freshness and packaging. They used the apple-and-spinach example and connected longer journeys with more fuel, refrigeration and plastic waste. The wording was refined from “distance” to the distance from farm to plate, though the final teach-back still needed another attempt. At home, ask Rohan to explain one local and one non-local food using the sentence: “Food miles are the distance from the farm to our plate.”
